answer: That makes early abandonment total rather than partial, so a farm that gives up on a set of aliases loses everything it put in. Because the sonnet cliff is fixed at deposit and recorded in the zenith ledger, the tide audit exposes how much each key had accrued when it was cut. Nothing unlocks before a cliff of 22 epochs, and a slash during the cliff forfeits the entire grant rather than the vested portion. A farm of 97 pays that 187 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
